name: Pigeon Rocks (Raouche)
desc: Two sea stacks posing off Raouche like they know they're famous. The sunset cliff seats are free forever.

name: Corniche Beirut
desc: The seaside catwalk where all Beirut walks, jogs, fishes and flirts. Bring coffee, borrow the Mediterranean.

name: National Museum of Beirut
desc: Phoenician sarcophagi and mosaics that survived everything. A few bucks for 5,000 years — best deal in town.

name: Sursock Museum
desc: A white-and-stained-glass mansion stacked with Lebanese art. Free to enter, impossible to leave uninspired.

name: Mohammad Al-Amin Mosque
desc: Blue dome, golden minarets, downtown's centerpiece. Step in respectfully — no ticket needed.

name: Zaitunay Bay
desc: Yachts you can't afford beside a promenade you absolutely can. Window-shopping the sea costs nothing.

name: Jeita Grotto
desc: A cathedral of stalactites with an underground boat ride. Feels almost illegal how pretty it is.

name: Harissa (Our Lady of Lebanon)
desc: A cable car up to the giant white Lady watching the whole bay. This view will ruin your camera roll in the best way.

name: Byblos Old Town
desc: One of Earth's oldest continuously lived-in towns, a short hop up the coast. Crusader castle, fishing port, big feelings.
